AP Macroeconomics.learning_target_s:
I can explain scarcity and why every choice has an opportunity cost (incl. explicit vs. implicit costs and marginal thinking).
I can construct and interpret a production possibilities curve (PPC) and show growth, contraction, efficiency, and increasing vs. constant opportunity cost.
I can distinguish positive from normative statements and explain how economists use models and assumptions (ceteris paribus).
I can compute absolute and comparative advantage from output or input data, identify the terms of trade that make both parties better off, and explain the gains from specialization.
I can describe the basic economic questions and how market vs. command systems answer them.

I can graph demand and supply, distinguish movement along a curve from a shift, and list the determinants of each.
I can find market equilibrium, explain how surpluses/shortages are eliminated, and predict the effect of single and double shifts on P and Q (incl. indeterminate outcomes).
I can analyze the effects of price ceilings/floors and simple taxes on a market graph.
I can use a world-price model to show gains/losses from trade and the effect of a tariff or quota.
PF: I can build and defend a monthly budget with fixed vs. variable expenses and a savings goal.

AP Macroeconomics.unit: UNIT 2 — Economic Indicators & the Business Cycle
AP Macroeconomics.learning_target_s:
I can draw the circular-flow model and explain why expenditure = income; I can compute GDP using the expenditure (C+I+G+NX) and income approaches and identify what is/isn't counted.
I can calculate real vs. nominal GDP, the GDP deflator, and real growth rates; I can explain the limitations of GDP as a measure of well-being.
I can compute CPI and inflation rate, distinguish CPI vs. deflator, and calculate real values/real wages; I can identify who wins and loses from unanticipated inflation/deflation.
I can compute unemployment and labor-force participation rates, classify frictional/structural/cyclical unemployment, and explain the natural rate.
I can label the phases of the business cycle and connect the output gap to cyclical unemployment.
PF: I can compare loan/insurance options using total cost, APR, and coverage.

AP Macroeconomics.unit: UNIT 3 — Long-Run Growth & the AD–AS Model
AP Macroeconomics.learning_target_s:
I can explain the sources of long-run growth (productivity, physical/human capital, technology, natural resources) and show growth as an outward PPC/LRAS shift; I can evaluate policies that promote growth.
I can graph AD, explain why it slopes down (wealth, interest-rate, exchange-rate effects), and list its shifters.
I can compute the spending multiplier and tax multiplier from MPC/MPS and use them to predict changes in real GDP.
I can graph SRAS and LRAS, explain their shapes and shifters, and identify long-run equilibrium at full employment.
I can use the AD–AS model to show recessionary and inflationary gaps, demand-pull vs. cost-push inflation, and stagflation, and explain the economy's long-run self-adjustment.
I can synthesize Units 1–3 for the semester midterm.

AP Macroeconomics.unit: UNIT 4A — Saving, Investment & the Financial System
AP Macroeconomics.learning_target_s:
I can describe financial institutions and markets and explain the difference between saving and investment; I can distinguish stocks, bonds, and other financial assets and the trade-offs of liquidity, risk, and return.
I can compute nominal vs. real interest rates (Fisher equation) and explain how expected inflation affects lenders and borrowers.
I can use national income accounting identities (S = I in a closed economy; national saving = private + public saving) and graph the loanable funds market to show effects of changes in saving, investment demand, and government budget deficits.
I can apply present value / compound interest, diversification, and risk-return concepts.
PF: I can open/manage checking & savings accounts, reconcile a statement, avoid fees, and explain retirement vehicles (401k, IRA, Roth) and the power of compounding.

I can define money, its functions, and the measures of the money supply (M1/M2), and distinguish commodity vs. fiat money.
I can construct bank balance sheets (T-accounts), compute required/excess reserves and the money multiplier, and trace how deposits expand the money supply.
I can graph the money market (nominal interest rate) and show effects of changes in money supply/demand.
I can explain the Fed's tools in BOTH a limited-reserves framework (OMOs, discount rate, reserve requirement) and an ample-reserves framework (interest on reserves, ON RRP, administered rates) and graph the reserve market.
I can use the quantity theory (MV = PY) and the equation of exchange to explain the long-run link between money growth and inflation, and explain the costs of inflation and monetary neutrality.
I can connect monetary policy → interest rates → investment → AD → output/price level.

AP Macroeconomics.unit: UNIT 5 — Fiscal & Monetary Policy, Inflation–Unemployment Trade-off, Deficits & Debt
AP Macroeconomics.learning_target_s:
I can explain discretionary fiscal policy (G and T changes) and automatic stabilizers, use multipliers to size a policy, and show fiscal policy in AD–AS.
I can compare expansionary/contractionary fiscal and monetary policy actions in the short run and their combined effects on output, price level, interest rates, and investment.
I can graph the short-run and long-run Phillips curves, relate them to AD–AS, and explain shifts due to supply shocks and changing expectations.
I can distinguish deficits from debt, explain how deficits are financed, and graph crowding out in the loanable funds market and its effect on long-run growth.
I can explain the long-run relationship between money growth and inflation and the classical dichotomy.
PF: I can complete a W-4 and 1040-EZ-style return and explain payroll taxes and filing obligations.

I can explain the balance of payments (current account, capital/financial account) and why they sum to zero; I can classify transactions.
I can define nominal and real exchange rates, appreciation/depreciation, and compute the effect on import/export prices.
I can graph the foreign exchange market for a currency and show shifts caused by changes in tastes, relative income, relative price levels, relative interest rates, and speculation.
I can trace how monetary/fiscal policy changes at home or abroad affect real interest rates, capital flows, the exchange rate, net exports, and AD.
I can integrate all models (AD–AS, money market, loanable funds, FX, Phillips curve) to analyze a full macroeconomic scenario from shock to policy response to long-run outcome.

AP Macroeconomics.unit: AP EXAM REVIEW → AP EXAM → CASE STUDY PROJECT & FINAL
AP Macroeconomics.learning_target_s:
I can recall and correctly draw every required macro graph (PPC, S&D, AD–AS, money market, reserve market, loanable funds, Phillips curve, FX market) with correct labels in under 2 minutes each.
I can complete an AP-length MC section (60 Qs / 70 min) and FRQ section (1 long + 2 short / 60 min) at proficiency.
I can analyze a country undergoing substantial economic change: define a research question, review sources, collect and interpret indicator data, evaluate leadership/policy choices, and present findings persuasively as a team (Case Study Project Phases 1–5).
I can relate current events to macroeconomic theory and defend conflicting economic viewpoints (LCCC obj. 4, 7, 9).

announcements.title: The CASTLE Program is looking for student volunteers
announcements.text: to join our Peer-Mediated Instruction and Intervention (PMII) program! Volunteers will spend 5th hour twice a month connecting with peers, participating in activities, and building meaningful social connections alongside students with autism. Interested in being part of PMII? Stop by A144 (CASTLE Lounge) to pick up a volunteer form or for additional info. Forms are due October 2nd!
